claim_text: OT loss and refinement efficacy: Claim that replacing LOT with MSE degrades drastically and removing refinement degrades 4.7 to 7.2. Bidirectional SW/EBSW OT loss and entropic adaptive refinement are necessary for best accuracy.
audit_scope: Audit scopes to claim-3 Table 4 ablation on SHREC19 after FAUST+SCAPE training: verifies arithmetic for LMSE vs LOT degradation and 4.7->7.2 refinement degradation, ranking/best-method, and whether bidirectional SW/EBSW textual claims match tabulated deltas. Audit does NOT cover: generalization beyond SHREC19, proper/fmap weight ablations, variance/significance (single run), hyperparameter search, actual code execution of SW/EBSW/Sinkhorn, or present-day SOTA status.

methodology_findings.finding: Author explicitly limits ablation generalizability to single train/test split (FAUST+SCAPE training, SHREC19 testing only).
methodology_findings.evidence: We train our model on FAUST+SCAPE dataset and evaluate it on SHREC19 dataset. // Table 4: Ablation study on SHREC19 // Limitations: Ablation only on SHREC19 after FAUST+SCAPE training

methodology_findings.finding: Entropic regularization sensitivity not reported: epsilon for p_epsilon=exp(-c/epsilon) / Sinkhorn iterations, number of slicing directions, uniform-sphere sampling parameters, and optimization hyperparameters for adaptive refinement not ablated or quantified.
methodology_findings.evidence: p_epsilon(x,y) proportional to exp(-1/epsilon c^2(x,y)) // projection operator of a given probability density p // Thanks to the differentiable property of the Sinkhorn algorithm, we can refine each individual pair by minimizing the Ltotal // no epsilon/iteration ablation in evidence bundle

methodology_findings.finding: Adaptive refinement is inference-only, applied once per pair due to quadratic memory; not used for large-scale training, limiting claims about train-time necessity and scalability.
methodology_findings.evidence: we only employ entropic OT for refinement once during the inference, thereby reducing the computation and memory cost of the Sinkhorn algorithm // Limitations: Used only once at inference due to quadratic memory; not used for large-scale training

methodology_findings.finding: Eq.10 LbiSW (bidirectional expectation over uniform slicing) and Eq.11 LbiEBSW (importance-weighted with w(theta)) and Eq.14 adaptive refinement via iterated Q-projections are internally consistent definitions; convergence to zero when soft similarity ~ permutation and cycle-consistency are definitional consequences, not numerically verified beyond Table 4 deltas; no equation-substitution numeric check possible.
methodology_findings.evidence: LbiSW = (E_theta~U(Sd-1)[Wp^p(thetaFx, thetaFy_hat)+Wp^p(thetaFy, thetaFx_hat)])^{1/p} // LbiEBSW = (E_theta~sigma0[ (Wtheta,X+Wtheta,Y) w(theta)] / E[w(theta)] )^{1/p} // ~Pi_xy = QX(QY...(QX(p_epsilon))) // The loss converges toward zero when the soft feature similarity hatPi approaches a (partial) permutation matrix... encourages the cycle consistency

methodology_findings.finding: Uniform slicing and importance-sampling limitations are author-acknowledged: uniform slicing may weight uninformative directions equally; EBSW requires importance sampling with added complexity, still needs empirical validation.
methodology_findings.evidence: Limitations: Uses uniform slicing which may weight uninformative directions equally. // Limitations: Requires importance sampling; added complexity vs vanilla SW, still needs empirical validation

cross_paper_findings.detail: Deep-shells f1 shows entropy-regularized OT energy integrating squared embedding distance enables differentiable Sinkhorn optimization (Eq.8), conceptually consistent with premise that OT-based distribution matching outperforms pointwise MSE. However f1 does not test this work's specific LOT (bidirectional SW/EBSW Eq.10/11) vs MSE degradation 34.3->4.7 nor refinement degradation 4.7->7.2, so cannot confirm magnitude or necessity of bidirectional SW/EBSW specifically.
cross_paper_findings.evidence: Eq. 8: OT energy integrating squared embedding distance under pi minus entropy regularization enables differentiable Sinkhorn optimization

cross_paper_findings.detail: Ground-cost construction and solver differ but are complementary: deep-shells Eq.10 encodes cost as Gibbs density p_lambda=exp(-scaled squared embedding distance) in R^{K+6} as Sinkhorn input with entropic iterations Eq.14 tilde Pi=QX(QY...(QX(p_epsilon))) (quadratic cost), vs this work Eq.10/11 SW/EBSW distance between feature distributions with soft-permuted features (closed-form). No contradiction; efficiency claims are complementary alternative entropic OT implementations.
cross_paper_findings.evidence: Eq. 10 defines p_lambda as exponential of negative scaled squared distance for Sinkhorn input

cross_paper_findings.detail: Deep-shells Eq.13 uses learned feature distance to compute initial pi as alternative ground cost, demonstrating OT performance is sensitive to cost definition - analogous to drastic 34.3->4.7 degradation when replacing LOT with MSE. However f3 shows sensitivity within OT variants, not MSE vs bidirectional SW/EBSW; single-dataset ablation alone is insufficient to claim necessity of bidirectional SW/EBSW over other feature-alignment losses, and provides no test of entropic adaptive refinement 4.7->7.2.
cross_paper_findings.evidence: Eq. 13: OT energy using learned feature distance to compute initial pi, showing alternative ground cost in same pipeline

cross_paper_findings.detail: f4 defines product-space embedding Eq.3 into R^{K+6} (intrinsic eigenfunctions plus extrinsic coordinates/normals) where Euclidean distance becomes OT ground cost. This is alternative feature space vs this work's soft-permuted feature distribution SW cost. Different metrics/assumptions and no LOT vs MSE or refinement ablation block direct comparison to necessity claims for bidirectional SW/EBSW and adaptive refinement.
cross_paper_findings.evidence: Eq. 3 embeds shape X into R^{K+6} using intrinsic eigenfunctions plus extrinsic smoothed coordinates and normals whose Euclidean distance becomes ground cost
